cards.subject: Physics
cards.topic: Gauss's law: infinitely long charged wire
cards.question: Using Gauss's law, derive the electric field due to an infinitely long straight uniformly charged wire.

items.label: Cylindrical Gaussian surface (coaxial, radius r, length l)
items.tip: Say 'cylindrical Gaussian surface' and draw it with r and l.

items.label: States Gauss's law (flux = q enclosed / ε0)
items.tip: Write: ∮E·dA = q/ε0.

items.label: Flux only through the curved surface (ends: E ⟂ dA, flux = 0)
items.tip: Say why the two flat ends give zero flux.

items.label: E (2πrl) = λl / ε0
items.tip: Write E × 2πrl = λl/ε0.

items.label: Final result E = λ / (2π ε0 r)
items.tip: Box the final answer.

cards.model: Take a cylindrical Gaussian surface of radius r and length l coaxial with the wire. By symmetry E is radial. Flux through the two flat ends is zero (E ⟂ dA). Through the curved surface flux = E(2πrl). By Gauss's law, total flux = q enclosed / ε0. Here E(2πrl) = λl/ε0, so E = λ/(2πε0 r).
mistakes: Forgetting to draw the Gaussian surface.
Not explaining why end flux is zero.
Dropping ε0 in the final answer.
cards.source: CBSE-style marking steps; teacher check pending.

cards.topic: Electric field on axial line of dipole
cards.question: Derive an expression for the electric field at a point on the axial line of an electric dipole of dipole moment p.

items.label: Defines dipole moment p = 2aq (from -q to +q)
items.tip: Define electric dipole moment p = 2aq directed from -q to +q.

items.label: Electric field components E+ and E- and subtraction
Final axial field for short dipole E = 2p / (4πε0 r^3)
items.tip: For r >> a, derive E = 2p/(4πε0 r^3).

cards.model: Electric dipole moment is p = 2aq directed from -q to +q. Electric field at point P on axial line: E+ = q / [4πε0 (r - a)^2] and E- = q / [4πε0 (r + a)^2]. Net field E = E+ - E- = (q/4πε0) [1/(r - a)^2 - 1/(r + a)^2] = (q/4πε0) [4ar / (r^2 - a^2)^2]. For a short dipole where r >> a, E = 2p / (4πε0 r^3) along the dipole axis.
mistakes: Writing 1/r^2 instead of 1/r^3 for dipole field.
Using the equatorial formula p/(4πε0 r^3) instead of axial formula 2p/(4πε0 r^3).

traps.msg: The axial field is twice the equatorial field: 2p/(4πε0 r^3), not p/(4πε0 r^3).

cards.question: State the principle of a moving coil galvanometer. How is a galvanometer converted into an ammeter of range 0 to I amperes?

items.label: Principle: Deflecting torque on current loop in magnetic field
items.tip: State that current loop in magnetic field experiences deflecting torque τ = NIAB.

items.label: Restoring couple Cθ gives I proportional to θ
items.tip: Equate NIAB = Cθ so current I is directly proportional to deflection θ.

items.label: Conversion to ammeter: Low resistance shunt S in parallel
items.tip: Connect a low resistance shunt S in parallel: S = (Ig · G) / (I - Ig).

cards.model: Principle: A current carrying coil placed in a uniform radial magnetic field experiences a deflecting torque τ = NIAB. A restoring torque Cθ balances it, giving NIAB = Cθ, so current I is directly proportional to deflection θ. To convert into an ammeter, connect a low resistance shunt S in parallel with the galvanometer. Shunt formula: S = (Ig G) / (I - Ig).

Forgetting that the magnetic field is made radial using concave poles and soft iron core.

traps.msg: Ammeter conversion requires a LOW resistance shunt in PARALLEL, not in series.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.question: Derive Lens Maker's formula: 1/f = (n - 1) (1/R1 - 1/R2) for a thin convex lens of radii of curvature R1 and R2.

items.label: Refraction at first surface: n2/v1 - n1/u = (n2 - n1)/R1
items.tip: Write refraction formula for surface 1: n2/v1 - n1/u = (n2 - n1)/R1.

items.label: Refraction at second surface: n1/v - n2/v1 = (n1 - n2)/R2
items.tip: Write refraction for surface 2 with virtual object: n1/v - n2/v1 = (n1 - n2)/R2.

items.label: Adds equations and applies 1/f = 1/v - 1/u to get 1/f = (n - 1)(1/R1 - 1/R2)
items.tip: Add equations and substitute 1/f = 1/v - 1/u to get 1/f = (n - 1)(1/R1 - 1/R2).

cards.model: Refraction at the first surface of the lens: n2/v1 - n1/u = (n2 - n1)/R1. Refraction at the second surface where I1 acts as virtual object: n1/v - n2/v1 = (n1 - n2)/R2 = - (n2 - n1)/R2. Adding both equations gives n1(1/v - 1/u) = (n2 - n1) (1/R1 - 1/R2). Since 1/v - 1/u = 1/f and n = n2/n1, we obtain Lens Maker's formula: 1/f = (n - 1) (1/R1 - 1/R2).
mistakes: Missing the negative sign when converting (n1 - n2)/R2 to - (n2 - n1)/R2.
Confusing R1 with R2.

traps.msg: Lens maker's formula has (1/R1 - 1/R2), not a plus sign.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.question: In Young's double slit experiment, deduce the condition for constructive interference and obtain the expression for fringe width β.

items.label: Path difference Δx = x d / D between two coherent waves
items.tip: Show path difference between slits S1 and S2 is Δx = xd / D.

items.label: Condition for maxima: xd / D = nλ gives x_n = nλD / d
items.tip: Constructive interference condition: Δx = nλ => x_n = nλD / d.

items.label: Fringe width β = x_(n+1) - x_n = λD / d
items.tip: Calculate separation between consecutive bright fringes: β = λD / d.

cards.model: In Young's double slit experiment, path difference between waves from slits S1 and S2 reaching point P is Δx = S2P - S1P = xd / D. For constructive interference (bright fringe), path difference Δx = nλ, where n = 0, 1, 2... Position of nth bright fringe is x_n = nλD / d. Fringe width β is the separation between two consecutive bright fringes: β = x_(n+1) - x_n = λD / d.
mistakes: Writing β = λd / D instead of λD / d.
Confusing slit separation d with screen distance D.

traps.msg: Fringe width is directly proportional to D: β = λD / d, not λd / D.

cards.topic: Full-wave rectifier using p-n junction diodes
cards.question: Draw the circuit diagram of a full-wave rectifier using two p-n junction diodes and explain its working.

items.label: Circuit: Center-tapped transformer with two diodes D1, D2 and load RL
items.tip: Mention center-tapped transformer, two diodes D1 and D2, and load resistor RL.

items.label: Positive half cycle: D1 is forward biased, D2 is reverse biased
items.tip: Explain: During positive half cycle, D1 conducts (forward biased) and D2 is reverse biased.
keys: positive half cycle: D1 forward biased, D2 reverse biased

items.label: Negative half cycle: D2 is forward biased; unidirectional current through RL
items.tip: During negative half cycle, D2 conducts; current through RL flows in the SAME direction.

cards.model: Circuit: A center-tapped secondary of an AC transformer is connected to two p-n junction diodes D1 and D2 with a load resistor RL connected to the center tap. Working: During the positive half cycle of AC input, diode D1 is forward biased and conducts while D2 is reverse biased. During the negative half cycle, diode D2 is forward biased and conducts while D1 is reverse biased. Current flows through the load resistor RL in the same unidirectional path during both cycles, producing rectified pulsating DC output.
mistakes: Stating that the output is pure DC (it is pulsating DC with ripple frequency 2f).
Forgetting the center-tapped connection of the secondary winding.

traps.msg: A full-wave rectifier produces pulsating DC; a filter capacitor is needed for pure DC.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.question: 18 g of glucose (C6H12O6, molar mass = 180 g/mol) is dissolved in 1 kg of water in a saucepan. At what temperature will water boil at 1.013 bar? (Kb for water = 0.52 K kg/mol, boiling point of pure water = 373.15 K).

items.label: Elevation formula ΔTb = Kb × m = Kb × (w2 / M2) × (1 / w1)
items.tip: Write formula ΔTb = Kb × m.

items.label: Calculates molality m = 0.1 mol/kg and ΔTb = 0.052 K
Final boiling point Tb = 373.15 + 0.052 = 373.202 K (with unit)
items.tip: Add ΔTb to 373.15 K to get Tb = 373.202 K.

cards.model: Formula for elevation in boiling point: ΔTb = Kb × m = Kb × (w2 / M2) × (1 / w1). Here w2 = 18 g, M2 = 180 g/mol, w1 = 1 kg. Molality m = (18 / 180) / 1 = 0.1 mol/kg. Elevation ΔTb = 0.52 K kg/mol × 0.1 mol/kg = 0.052 K. Boiling point of solution Tb = Tb° + ΔTb = 373.15 K + 0.052 K = 373.202 K.
mistakes: Giving ΔTb (0.052 K) as the final boiling point without adding it to 373.15 K.
Subtracting ΔTb instead of adding it.

traps.msg: Boiling point ELEVATES (increases), so add ΔTb to pure boiling point, do not subtract.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.question: Calculate the EMF of the cell at 298 K: Mg(s) | Mg2+(0.001 M) || Cu2+(0.0001 M) | Cu(s). Given: E°(Mg2+/Mg) = -2.37 V, E°(Cu2+/Cu) = +0.34 V.

items.label: Standard EMF E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = 0.34 - (-2.37) = 2.71 V (n = 2)
Nernst equation formula: Ecell = E°cell - (0.059/n) log([Mg2+]/[Cu2+])
items.tip: Write Ecell = E°cell - (0.059/2) log([Mg2+]/[Cu2+]).

items.label: Calculates log(10) = 1 and final Ecell = 2.68 V (with unit)

cards.model: Cell reaction: Mg(s) + Cu2+(aq) -> Mg2+(aq) + Cu(s) with n = 2 electrons transferred. Standard cell potential E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = 0.34 V - (-2.37 V) = 2.71 V. According to Nernst equation at 298 K: Ecell = E°cell - (0.059 / 2) log([Mg2+] / [Cu2+]). Concentration ratio = 0.001 / 0.0001 = 10, so log(10) = 1. Ecell = 2.71 - 0.0295 × 1 = 2.68 V.
mistakes: Using n = 1 instead of n = 2 in Nernst equation.
Inverting the ion ratio as [Cu2+]/[Mg2+] instead of [anode]/[cathode].

traps.msg: The log ratio is [Mg2+]/[Cu2+] = 10, so you must subtract 0.0295 V, not add it.

items.tip: Write IUPAC name: hexaamminecobalt(III) ion (note spelling: double m).

items.label: Co3+ (3d6), NH3 pairs electrons -> d2sp3 hybridization, octahedral geometry
items.tip: State d2sp3 hybridization, octahedral geometry (inner orbital complex).

items.label: Diamagnetic (no unpaired electrons)
items.tip: State diamagnetic because all electrons are paired.

cards.model: 1. IUPAC name: hexaamminecobalt(III) ion. 2. Oxidation state of Co is +3 with electronic configuration [Ar] 3d6. In presence of NH3 (a strong field ligand), electrons in 3d pair up completely leaving two empty 3d orbitals. These hybridize with 4s and three 4p orbitals to form d2sp3 hybridization giving an octahedral inner orbital complex. 3. Magnetic property: Since there are no unpaired electrons, the complex is diamagnetic.

Writing sp3d2 instead of d2sp3 (it is an inner orbital complex).

traps.msg: [Co(NH3)6]3+ is d2sp3 and diamagnetic, not outer-orbital sp3d2 or paramagnetic.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.question: Differentiate between Aldol Condensation and Cannizzaro Reaction with respect to: (i) Essential structural feature, (ii) Reagent used, (iii) Nature of products formed.

items.label: Structural feature: Aldol requires α-hydrogen; Cannizzaro requires absence of α-hydrogen
items.tip: Aldol needs at least one α-hydrogen; Cannizzaro occurs in aldehydes lacking α-hydrogen.

items.label: Reagent: Aldol uses dilute alkali; Cannizzaro uses concentrated alkali (50% NaOH)
items.tip: Aldol uses dilute base (dil. NaOH); Cannizzaro uses concentrated base (conc. 50% NaOH).

items.label: Products: Aldol gives β-hydroxy aldehyde; Cannizzaro gives alcohol and carboxylic acid salt
items.tip: Aldol yields β-hydroxy aldehyde (or α,β-unsaturated enal); Cannizzaro disproportionates to alcohol + salt.

cards.model: 1. Structural requirement: Aldol condensation requires aldehydes or ketones having at least one α-hydrogen atom (e.g. CH3CHO). Cannizzaro reaction requires aldehydes with the absence of α-hydrogen atoms (e.g. HCHO, C6H5CHO). 2. Reagent: Aldol uses dilute alkali (dil. NaOH or Ba(OH)2). Cannizzaro uses concentrated alkali (50% conc. NaOH). 3. Products: Aldol forms a β-hydroxy aldehyde (aldol) which upon heating eliminates water to form an α,β-unsaturated aldehyde. Cannizzaro undergoes disproportionation yielding an alcohol and a salt of carboxylic acid.
mistakes: Confusing dilute alkali in Aldol with concentrated alkali in Cannizzaro.
Saying ketones can undergo Cannizzaro reaction (only aldehydes lacking α-hydrogen).

traps.msg: Cannizzaro requires CONCENTRATED alkali (50% NaOH); Aldol requires DILUTE base.

cards.subject: Biology
cards.question: Describe the biological (secondary) treatment of sewage water. How does it reduce BOD?

items.label: Aeration tanks with continuous mechanical agitation and air pumped in
items.tip: Primary effluent passes into large aeration tanks with vigorous mechanical agitation.

items.label: Growth of aerobic microbes into flocs (bacteria + fungal filaments)
items.tip: Vigorous growth of useful aerobic microbes forming flocs (bacteria associated with fungal filaments).

items.label: Microbes consume organic matter reducing BOD; flocs settle as activated sludge
items.tip: Microbes consume organic matter, greatly reducing BOD; effluent passes to settling tank where flocs sediment as activated sludge.

cards.model: Primary effluent is transferred into large aeration tanks where it is constantly mechanically agitated and air is pumped into it. This allows vigorous growth of useful aerobic microbes into flocs (masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments to form mesh-like structures). While growing, these aerobic microbes consume the major part of organic matter in the effluent, significantly reducing BOD (Biological Oxygen Demand). The effluent is then passed into a settling tank where the bacterial flocs settle down to form activated sludge.
mistakes: Calling microbes in aeration tank anaerobic (they are AEROBIC).
Thinking BOD increases during treatment (BOD decreases as pollution drops).

traps.msg: Microbes in the aeration tank are AEROBIC, and treatment REDUCES the BOD.

cards.subject: Biology
cards.question: Explain co-dominance with reference to the inheritance of ABO blood groups in humans.

items.label: Gene I with three alleles: IA, IB, and i
items.tip: ABO blood groups are controlled by gene I having three alleles: IA, IB, and i.

items.label: IA and IB produce sugars; allele i produces no sugar; IA and IB dominant over i
items.tip: IA and IB produce different sugars on RBC surface; allele i produces no sugar; IA and IB are dominant over i.
keys: IA and IB dominant over i

items.label: Genotype IAIB: Both alleles express equally producing AB blood type (co-dominance)
items.tip: When IA and IB are present together (IAIB), both express equally resulting in AB blood group.

cards.model: Human ABO blood groups are controlled by gene I with three alleles: IA, IB, and i. Alleles IA and IB produce slightly different forms of sugar polymers on RBC membranes, while allele i does not produce any sugar. IA and IB are completely dominant over allele i. However, when both IA and IB are present together in an individual (genotype IAIB), both alleles express their own types of sugars equally without blending. This phenomenon is called co-dominance, resulting in blood group AB.
mistakes: Confusing co-dominance with incomplete dominance (in co-dominance, both phenotypes are expressed equally, not blended).
Thinking that the i allele produces a different type of sugar (it produces no sugar).

traps.msg: Blood group AB is an example of CO-DOMINANCE, not incomplete dominance or blending.

items: ABO blood group system is controlled by multiple alleles of gene I
Three alleles: IA and IB (dominant), and i (recessive)
IA produces sugar antigen A; IB produces sugar antigen B; i produces neither
In heterozygote IAIB, both sugars are produced in equal measure
Because both alleles are simultaneously expressed, it is co-dominant

cards.subject: Biology
cards.question: Describe the three main steps of Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR). Name the thermostable enzyme used and its source organism.

items.label: Step 1: Denaturation at high temperature (~94°C) to separate dsDNA
items.tip: Denaturation: High temperature (~94°C) breaks H-bonds to separate dsDNA.

items.label: Step 2: Annealing of primers (~54°C) and Step 3: Extension by DNA polymerase (~72°C)
items.tip: Annealing: Primers bind at ~54°C. Extension: Polymerase extends primers with dNTPs at ~72°C.

items.label: Thermostable enzyme Taq polymerase from Thermus aquaticus
items.tip: Taq polymerase isolated from bacterium Thermus aquaticus remains active at high temperatures.

cards.model: PCR amplifies a specific DNA segment in three steps: 1. Denaturation: Double-stranded target DNA is heated to high temperature (~94°C) to separate the two strands. 2. Annealing: Two sets of oligonucleotide primers bind to complementary regions at ~54°C. 3. Extension: Thermostable DNA polymerase extends the primers using dNTPs at ~72°C. The thermostable enzyme used is Taq polymerase, isolated from the thermophilic bacterium Thermus aquaticus, which remains stable at high temperatures.
mistakes: Using human DNA polymerase (it gets denatured at 94°C).
Misspelling the source organism Thermus aquaticus.

traps.msg: PCR uses thermostable Taq DNA polymerase from Thermus aquaticus, not RNA polymerase or ligase.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.question: Evaluate the definite integral using properties: I = ∫_0^(π/2) [√sin x / (√sin x + √cos x)] dx.

items.label: Applies property ∫_0^a f(x)dx = ∫_0^a f(a - x)dx
items.tip: Apply P4 property to replace x with (π/2 - x): I = ∫_0^(π/2) [√cos x / (√cos x + √sin x)] dx.

items.label: Adds equations (1) and (2) to get 2I = ∫_0^(π/2) 1 dx
items.tip: Add both equations: 2I = ∫_0^(π/2) [(√sin x + √cos x)/(√sin x + √cos x)] dx = ∫_0^(π/2) 1 dx.

items.label: Integrates: 2I = [x]_0^(π/2) = π/2 giving I = π/4
items.tip: Evaluate 2I = π/2 - 0 => I = π/4.

cards.model: Let I = ∫_0^(π/2) [√sin x / (√sin x + √cos x)] dx ... (1). Using property ∫_0^a f(x) dx = ∫_0^a f(a - x) dx, we substitute x with (π/2 - x): I = ∫_0^(π/2) [√sin(π/2 - x) / (√sin(π/2 - x) + √cos(π/2 - x))] dx = ∫_0^(π/2) [√cos x / (√cos x + √sin x)] dx ... (2). Adding equations (1) and (2) gives 2I = ∫_0^(π/2) [(√sin x + √cos x) / (√sin x + √cos x)] dx = ∫_0^(π/2) 1 dx. Thus 2I = [x]_0^(π/2) = π/2 - 0 = π/2, which gives I = π/4.
mistakes: Forgetting to divide by 2 at the final step (writing π/2 instead of π/4).
Forgetting to state the property ∫_0^a f(x) dx = ∫_0^a f(a-x) dx.

traps.msg: Do not forget that the sum of the two integrals equals 2I, so I = (π/2) / 2 = π/4.

cards.subject: Accountancy
cards.question: State whether the following transactions result in inflow, outflow, or no flow of cash and cash equivalents: (i) Purchase of machinery by issue of equity shares of ₹5,00,000, (ii) Cash received from trade receivables ₹80,000, (iii) Sale of investment (cost ₹60,000) for ₹75,000.

items.label: (i) Issue of shares for machinery: No flow (non-cash transaction)
items.tip: State "No flow" because it is a non-cash investing/financing transaction.

items.label: (ii) Cash from trade receivables: Inflow from Operating Activities ₹80,000
items.tip: Cash received from debtors is an Inflow under Operating Activities.

items.label: (iii) Sale of investment: Inflow from Investing Activities ₹75,000
items.tip: Gross proceeds ₹75,000 are an Inflow under Investing Activities.

cards.model: (i) Purchase of machinery by issue of equity shares: No flow of cash. This is a non-cash transaction since neither cash nor cash equivalents are involved. (ii) Cash received from trade receivables ₹80,000: Inflow of cash under Operating Activities. (iii) Sale of investment for ₹75,000: Inflow of cash ₹75,000 under Investing Activities (the gross proceeds are recorded under investing activities).
mistakes: Classifying issue of shares for machinery as a financing inflow (it does not involve cash).
Reporting only the ₹15,000 gain under investing rather than the full ₹75,000 proceeds.

cards.subject: Accountancy
cards.topic: Current ratio and quick ratio calculation
cards.question: Current Assets of a company are ₹3,00,000 and Current Liabilities are ₹1,50,000. If Inventories are ₹60,000 and Prepaid Expenses are ₹15,000, calculate: (i) Current Ratio, (ii) Quick Ratio. State the ideal norm for both.

items.label: Current Ratio = 3,00,000 / 1,50,000 = 2:1 (ideal norm 2:1)
items.tip: Current Ratio = CA / CL = 3,00,000 / 1,50,000 = 2:1. Ideal norm is 2:1.

items.label: Quick Assets = CA - Inventories - Prepaid Expenses = ₹2,25,000
Quick Ratio = 2,25,000 / 1,50,000 = 1.5:1 (ideal norm 1:1)
items.tip: Quick Ratio = 2,25,000 / 1,50,000 = 1.5:1. Ideal norm is 1:1.

cards.model: 1. Current Ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities = 3,00,000 / 1,50,000 = 2:1. The ideal norm for current ratio is 2:1. 2. Quick Assets = Current Assets - Inventories - Prepaid Expenses = 3,00,000 - 60,000 - 15,000 = ₹2,25,000. 3. Quick Ratio = Quick Assets / Current Liabilities = 2,25,000 / 1,50,000 = 1.5:1 (or 3:2). The ideal norm for quick ratio is 1:1.
mistakes: Deducting only inventories and forgetting to deduct prepaid expenses.
Expressing ratios as decimals (1.5) without the ":1" ratio format.

traps.msg: Remember to deduct BOTH inventories (₹60,000) AND prepaid expenses (₹15,000) from Current Assets.
